title: Rotation cushioning and stateful drain coordinator
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets experience short SLO blips and KV-cache cold starts during node rotations, rolling upgrades, and maintenance windows. Existing drain flows are stateless and optimized for eviction speed, but for latency-sensitive tenants (throughput guarantees) we need graceful state preservation and a temporary capacity cushion to avoid throughput regression when nodes are removed.

This ticket proposes a 'rotation cushioning' mechanism combined with a 'stateful drain coordinator' that: (1) reserves a transient buffer of capacity (cushion) to absorb load during node removal/upgrade; (2) orchestrates multi-phase drains that checkpoint and preserve per-tenant KV cache or prefix caches where feasible; (3) integrates with autoscaler to provision hedging nodes on short notice and release them automatically; (4) exposes controls to Dedicated customers to set cushion size, allowed preheat time, and maintenance window policies.

Key goals: preserve token-level latency SLOs during maintenance, minimize cold-started KV miss rates, keep additional cost (cushion) predictable, and provide observability on cushion usage and drain progress.

Non-goals: full application-level snapshot/restore for arbitrary stateful workloads (out of scope), heavy-weight per-request checkpointing that would slow serving runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Rotation cushion can be configured per-fleet and per-tenant as an absolute slot count or percent
Stateful drain coordinator exposes a 3-phase drain (quiesce -> checkpoint -> evict) with metricized progress
Autoscaler can provision hedging nodes within configured preheat time and mark cushion capacity in the routing plane
End-to-end test simulating a rolling upgrade shows <5% latency tail increase and <10% increase in per-token cost for affected tenants
Observability dashboard shows cushion utilization, KV-checkpoint success rate, and a timeline of drain phases
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind fleet-level toggle. 2) Start with 10 internal Dedicated fleets (canary) for 2 weeks. 3) Expand to customers that opt-in via Console with guided defaults. 4) Monitor cushion utilization, tail latency, and cost delta; roll back on regression >10% p99 or sustained cushion >80%.

2026-03-03 - Design review (Diana Chen): suggested adding a 'preheat' phase where newly-provisioned hedging nodes receive synthetic KV-warmup traffic for common prefixes to reduce miss rate. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-06 - Security (Rajan Iyer): called out KMS usage for checkpoint metadata and audit logs; no sensitive payloads stored, only opaque cache digests. Marked security_review_required=false but flagged for ops review.

2026-03-10 - QA (Leah Moreno): integration test matrix outlined: single-hosted tenant, multi-tenant sharing KV pools, autoscaler-triggered cushion; identified a race where rapid repeated drains double-count cushion — added mitigation task ENG-224584.
